Hosted worlds keep real time: the host no longer searches the game's whole object list several times a second.

## Server

### Changed
- `mods.txt` switches on only `SolarpunkServerRuntime`, and the bundle check fails a bundle that switches a UE4SS sample mod on.
- Every 5 minutes the host log gets a `scan stats` line: how many object searches ran and why.
- MessagePack 3.1.9 (security advisory GHSA-qhrr-8q5h-9q3h; not reachable in Sundial: the only decode is the supervisor's owner-only named pipe, HMAC-checked first, into fixed record types).

### Fixed
- Worlds ran at about 95-96.5% of real time, even with nobody on. The host mods searched the game's whole object list twice every 250 ms (the player controllers and the game state), and the server runs a fixed 30 fps step, so every stalled frame was world time lost. Found objects are now kept between ticks and searched again only after a map load, when one is gone, when a player joins or leaves, and every 30 seconds (single objects every 2 minutes): about 0.08 searches a second instead of 8.3. Measured on a test server: 99.30% to 99.90% of real time with nobody on, 99.08% to 99.91% with two players, and the game process used about 30% less CPU.
- On `"Transport": "eos"` a configured `SolarpunkAuthPassword` kicked every player once the 120-second grace ran out, because players who join with the invite code cannot send the password. On eos the invite code is the gate: the password is set aside (and logged), the watchdog no longer stops the server over it, and the query reply no longer advertises a password. The address transport is unchanged.

Players need nothing installed: in Solarpunk choose Multiplayer, Join session, Enter Code, and type the server's 5-letter code.
